extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, practitioners (attorneys/agents), and USPTO examiners/staff involved in appeal practice
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for preparing and filing an appeal brief and related appeal-stage practice before the USPTO Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences/Patent Trial & Appeal Board (MPEP guidance). Covers timing, required content, record definitions, interviews, remands, and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Appeal Review Possible Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel decision outcomes: (A) The panel may affirm the rejection as to the issue for appeal; (B) Prosecution on the merits is reopened and an appropriate Office communication will follow; (C) The application is allowed on the existing claims and prosecution remains closed; (D) The request fails to comply with the submission requirements and is dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In appropriate circumstances the panel may propose changes or accompany its decision with a proposed amendment that, if accepted, may result in indication of allowability for contested claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filings That Terminate Pre-Appeal Panel Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The panel’s review will be terminated if the applicant files any of the following after filing a pre-appeal request but prior to a panel decision: (A) an appeal brief; (B) a request for continued examination (RCE); (C) an after-final amendment; (D) an affidavit or other evidence; (E) an express abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any of these are filed before the panel issues its decision, panel review ends and normal prosecution/appeal timelines follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Pre-Appeal Review on Appeal Brief Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: After a panel decision, the time period for filing an appeal brief is reset to one month from the mailing of the decision on the request, or to the balance of the two-month period running from receipt of the notice of appeal, whichever is greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing period for the appeal brief following a panel decision is extendible under 37 CFR 1.136. For as long as the pilot remains in effect, filing a pre-appeal request may extend the appeal brief filing period until a decision is made or the request is dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews After Notice of Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: One interview after final rejection is normally permitted (the period 'after final rejection' runs from the mailing of the final rejection through filing of the appeal brief). No interviews will be granted from filing of a pre-appeal review request through issuance of a decision on the request. Except in unusual situations, no interview is permitted after the appeal brief is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews during the period after mailing of an examiner's answer but prior to payment of the forwarding fee are likely to confuse the record and are not permitted except in unusual circumstances (e.g., appellant wishes to cancel all appealed claims and proceed to issue, or examiner convinced some claims are in condition for allowance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remand and Authority for Interviews on Board-Jurisdiction Cases
rubrics_metrics.description: After the time specified in 37 CFR 41.35(a), the examiner no longer has jurisdiction; the Director or delegate has authority to remand under 37 CFR 41.35(c). Requests for interviews on cases under Board jurisdiction should be granted only with specific approval of the Technology Center Director upon a written showing of extraordinary circumstances justifying a remand to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remand is exceptional and requires written justification demonstrating extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Evidence (appeal context)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of this subpart, 'Evidence' means something (including testimony, documents and tangible objects) that tends to prove or disprove the existence of an alleged fact, except that Evidence does not include dictionaries, which may be cited before the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluding dictionaries from 'Evidence' allows parties and examiners to cite them in briefs/answers without invoking rules that treat submitted materials as evidence; case law (e.g., Phillips, Nix v. Hedden) supports consulting dictionaries as aids to understanding rather than formal evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Record / Official Record on Appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Record' consists of items listed in the content listing of the Image File Wrapper (IFW) of the official file (or the official file if other than IFW), excluding amendments, Evidence, and documents that were not entered or indicated considered by the examiner. In reissued or reexamined patents, the Record includes the Record of the patent being reissued or reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical items not scanned into IFW (e.g., original design drawings, sequence listings) are included via content listing entries pointing to artifact files. References listed on an Information Disclosure Statement that have been indicated as considered by the examiner, or on form PTO-892, are included in the Record even if not separately appearing in the IFW content listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of IDS Held in Abeyance
rubrics_metrics.description: An information disclosure statement or petition held in abeyance while the Board has jurisdiction is not an entered or indicated considered document and is therefore excluded from the definition of 'Record' until entered or indicated to have been considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refusal to enter an amendment/evidence is petitionable and not subject to Board review; the Record reflects only entered and indicated-considered documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to File Appeal Brief and Fee Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant must file a brief within two months from the date of filing the notice of appeal under 37 CFR 41.31. Effective March 19, 2013 the appeal brief fee in an application or ex parte reexamination is set to $0. Failure to file within the period will result in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The measuring date is the Office date of receipt of the notice of appeal (not Certificate of Mailing dates except in certain USPS Priority Mail Express deposit-date rules). The brief cannot be filed within the time allowed for reply to the action from which the appeal was taken if that time is later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Brief Required Content (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal brief must contain the items set forth in 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1) under appropriate headings and in the specified order: (i) real party in interest; (ii) related appeals/interferences/trials; (iii) summary of claimed subject matter; (iv) argument; (v) claims appendix. A brief filed by an appellant not represented by a registered practitioner need only substantially comply with (i), (ii), (iv), and (v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief must set forth arguments and the basis with citations of statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the Record relied on. Arguments or authorities not included in the appeal brief will be refused consideration (with specified exceptions). Headings may be omitted if an item is not applicable (e.g., inventor is real party in interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Real Party in Interest Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by name the real party in interest at the time the appeal brief is filed is required, except when the named inventor(s) are themselves the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If omitted, the Office may assume the named inventor(s) are the real party in interest. Identification helps the Board comply with ethics rules to avoid conflicts. Examples: identify assignee and parent/affiliate structures when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Appeals / Cases Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement identifying by application, patent, appeal, interference, or trial number all other prior and pending appeals, interferences, trials before the Board, or judicial proceedings that (a) involve an application/patent owned by the appellant or assignee, (b) are known to appellant/legal representative/assignee, and (c) may be related to, directly affect or be directly affected by or have a bearing on the Board’s decision (collectively 'related cases').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no related cases exist, the statement is not required; omission may be taken as indicating no related cases. Copies of decisions in related cases are not required to be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Claimed Subject Matter Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each rejected independent claim, with references to the specification in the Record by page/line or paragraph and to drawings by reference characters. For means-plus-function (35 U.S.C. 112(f)) claims, identify corresponding structure/material/acts in the specification with references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to the patent application publication does not satisfy the requirement. Each rejected independent claim must be summarized concisely so the Board can readily see what is being contested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument Content and Presentation Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments must address each ground of rejection and the basis therefor, with citations to statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the Record relied on, explaining why the examiner erred for each contested ground. Each ground contested must be argued under a separate heading that reasonably identifies the ground (e.g., claim number, statutory basis, applied reference).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments or authorities not included in the brief will be refused consideration by the Board for the present appeal (except as provided in 37 CFR §§ 41.41, 41.47, 41.52). For multiple claims under the same ground, appellant may argue claims separately, as a group, or as a subgroup; failure to separately argue a grouped claim constitutes waiver of an argument that the Board must consider patentability of any grouped claim separately. Mere restatement of what a claim recites is not an argument. The Board may select a single claim from a group to decide the appeal on that basis. New arguments made first at oral hearing are normally not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping Claims and Waiver Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: When multiple claims are subject to the same ground of rejection, claims may be argued separately, as a group (stand or fall together), or as a subgroup. Failure to separately argue claims grouped together constitutes a waiver of any argument that the Board must consider the patentability of any grouped claim separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant groups claims, the Board may elect to decide based on a single selected claim from the group or subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Appendix Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal must be included with the appeal brief (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one copy of the appeal brief is required; although an evidence appendix is no longer required, the claims appendix is mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: No New or Non-Admitted Amendments/Evidence in Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other Evidence. Post-final amendments/evidence filed under 37 CFR 1.116 or 41.33 will not be entered into the appeal record unless entered by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of an examiner's refusal to admit amendment or evidence is by petition to the Director (37 CFR 1.181). See rules governing treatment of such submissions filed after final action but before/at filing of an appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Non-Compliance and Cure Period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with all requirements of 37 CFR 41.37(c), the appellant will be notified of reasons for non-compliance and given a time period to file an amended brief. Failure to timely file an amended brief that overcomes stated deficiencies results in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review of a determination of non-compliance is by petition to the Chief Administrative Patent Judge (37 CFR 41.3). For briefs filed on/after Jan 23, 2012, non-compliant briefs are held non-compliant under 37 CFR 41.37(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of Time for Filing the Appeal Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2-month period for filing an appeal brief may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a) (and (b) for extraordinary circumstances) for patent applications, and under 37 CFR 1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination proceedings. Additional time in excess of 5 months will not be granted unless extraordinary circumstances are shown under 1.136(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a proper petition for extension is filed, the new due date is computed from the receipt date of the notice of appeal. Petitions for extension require payment of the appropriate fees. Example computations (calendar rules, holiday/weekend adjustments) are provided in the MPEP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro Se (Unrepresented) Brief Content Leniency
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief filed by an appellant who is not represented by a registered practitioner and not prepared or signed by a registered practitioner need only substantially comply with paragraphs (c)(1)(i) (real party), (c)(1)(ii) (related cases), (c)(1)(iv) (argument), and (c)(1)(v) (claims appendix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will accept a pro se brief that substantially complies with those specified subparagraphs even if other technical requirements are not strictly followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence Appendix Recommendation and Identification of Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Although no longer required, the Office strongly encourages and appreciates receiving copies of the evidence relied upon (e.g., copies of declarations, affidavits, evidence of secondary considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not provided, appellants should clearly identify in the brief the evidence relied upon, with a clear description and the date of entry into the Image File Wrapper, to ensure the Board considers the proper evidence and avoid confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Contained Brief Requirement; No Incorporation by Reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief should fully state appellant’s position with respect to each ground of rejection so that no search of the Record is required; it should not incorporate or reference previous responses. Oral argument will not remedy deficiencies in a brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board expects a self-contained presentation with citations to the Record; insufficient briefs may be held non-compliant and lead to dismissal if not corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality and Limits on New Arguments/Authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in 37 CFR §§ 41.41, 41.47 and 41.52, any arguments or authorities not included in the appeal brief will be refused consideration by the Board for purposes of the present appeal. New arguments made for the first time at oral hearing are normally not entitled to consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental briefs or documents may be filed if new authority becomes available after filing (e.g., a pertinent court decision published after the brief). The rule is limited to the present appeal and does not preclude arguments in subsequent appeals in the same application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Technology Center and Application Number on Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Every document relating to an appeal, including the brief, should indicate the number of the Technology Center (TC) to which the application or patent under reexamination is assigned and the application or reexamination control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This facilitates routing and consideration by the correct Board members and staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of Failure to Timely File an Appeal Brief; Revival/Reinstatement Options
rubrics_metrics.description: If the brief is not filed within the prescribed period (or extended period), the appeal ordinarily will be dismissed. If any claims stand allowed, the application does not become abandoned but is returned to the examiner for action on allowed claims; if there are no allowed claims, the application is abandoned as of the date the brief was due. In ex parte reexamination, failure to file results in issuance of the certificate under 37 CFR 1.570.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If application is abandoned, applicant may petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137 (with showing/fee). If appeal dismissed but application not abandoned due to at least one allowed claim, appellant may file a petition to reinstate claims and the appeal, requiring an equivalent showing to revive and filing either an RCE (with submission/reply and fee) or an appeal brief (and filing fee where applicable). Filing a petition pointing out an erroneous dismissal may be sufficient if dismissal was in error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to File Appeal Brief After Revival
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is revived after abandonment for failure to file an appeal brief and the petition to revive was accompanied by a notice of appeal, appellant has two months from the mailing date of the Director's affirmative decision on the petition in which to file the appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136 as applicable.
